 Early voting numbers show strong Democratic turnout in Louisiana 
 A sign directing voters to an early voting location in the Lake Vista neighborhood of New Orleans. (WVUE-TV) By Thanh Truong Published : Oct. 26, 2026 at 4:12 PM CDT | Updated : 3 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - Democratic turnout has been higher than Republican turnout in Louisiana’s early voting period, but one political analyst said the GOP will prevail in the race between Democratic Senate candidate Jamie Davis and Republican Senate candidate Julia Letlow. 
 According to data from the Louisiana Secretary of State’s office, more 363,685 people voted in the first five days of Louisiana’s early voting period this year. 
 LSU New Orleans political analyst Ed Chervenak said the first week of early voting almost topped the state’s early voting total from 2022. 
 “We have two more days of early voting, so we’ll surpass what we turned out four years ago,” said Ed Chervenak, political analyst at LSU New Orleans. 
 A breakdown of Louisiana’s early voting so far by the University of Florida’s Election Lab shows 43% are registered Democrats, 39% are registered Republicans and 17% have minor or no party affiliation. 
 Leaders of Louisiana’s Democratic Party said they’re seeing significant early voting gains from the previous midterm election, and they’re looking to boost turnout in Democratic leaning cities like New Orleans and Baton Rouge. 
 “We’re going to focus and put direct action in all those areas that we believe that we can increase the voter turnout, including East Baton Rouge,” said Randal Gaines, chairman of the Louisiana Democratic Party. 
 Fox 8 reached out to the GOP in Louisiana to comment on the early voting results, but did not get a reply as of 4 p.m. on Oct. 26. 
 Chervenak said enthusiasm among Black voters appears to be high. The Republican effort to redraw election maps this year is part of the reason why Black voters have been energized, Chervenak claimed.
 “I believe that the redistricting decisions did motivate Blacks because they feel like now their vote is being diluted. And so, here’s a chance for them to show up and cast ballots and basically illustrate their vote does matter,” said Dr. Chervenak. 
 Despite the reported Democratic enthusiasm in early voting, Chervenak said it likely won’t be enough to determine the race between Democrat Jamie Davis and Republican Julia Letlow to represent Louisiana in the U.S. Senate. 
 “The predictive market basically gives Julia Letlow a 92% likelihood of winning. Even though she may be only four points up in the polls, the money is on Letlow to win this,” Chervenak said. 
 While Democrats may be showing up in bigger numbers during early voting, Dr. Chervenak said Republicans historically have stronger turnout on Election Day.
 Come Nov. 3, Chervenak said he expects Republicans to show why Louisiana remains red. Early voting in Louisiana ends Tuesday evening (Oct. 27).
